plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flattened stems that have pointed teeth along the edges. It produces tubular, asymmetrical flowers at the tips of the stems. It is widely grown as a houseplant in the Northern Hemisphere, where it flowers as nights lengthen and temperatures cool.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: It is a short-day plant, so it needs long nights of about 12-14 hours of darkness to set flower buds. It can live for decades and is often passed down through families.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves and large clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Mass blooms cover the canopy and carpet the ground beneath with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, giving it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. In Australia, an old tradition holds that a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often lightly fragrant flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and tolerates more sun. Its flowers are single to semi-double with prominent yellow stamens, and it provides valuable nectar for pollinators in late autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan and southern China; grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua petals fall individually, unlike Camellia japonica, which often drops whole blooms. Its seeds can be pressed to produce tea seed oil used for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Poinsettia (Euphorbia pulcherrima)
plants.description: A woody shrub that grows up to 3 meters in warm climates. What appear to be petals are actually colorful bracts surrounding small yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In the Northern Hemisphere it is a popular holiday plant, while in frost-free regions it grows outdoors and displays color in late autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in tropical and subtropical regions and indoors elsewhere
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it Cuetlaxochitl and used the sap to make a fever medicine and the bracts to make a reddish dye. Like the Thanksgiving cactus, it needs long nights to develop its bract color.
